claire: Heads up 9: I noticed the API reference still shows a JSON body for POST /v1/uploads in the "request example" block. Our server prefers multipart/form-data for binary files and the JSON example is misleading. Opened PR #3599 to swap the canonical example to multipart and add a short Python requests + browser FormData snippet.

sam: thanks, ran into this during a quick smoke test too. server returns 415 when `Content-Type: application/json` is used for binary bytes.

docs-bot: PR #3599 by claire: docs(upload): make multipart canonical, add curl/python/js examples, update OpenAPI requestBody, add migration note. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3599 :sparkles:

adrien: a couple of asks for the PR: 1) Add `multipart/form-data` to OpenAPI requestBody with `file: type: string, format: binary` and `purpose: {type: string, enum: ["semantic_search","vector_index","document_ingest"]}`. 2) Update the response example: runtime now returns `storage_key` and `metadata` (not `file_id`). I'll handle the OpenAPI patch if you push the markdown.

claire: planned examples in the PR:
- curl (canonical):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -F "file=@./sample.pdf" \
  -F "purpose=document_ingest"
```
- Python requests: ``requests.post(url, headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {key}'}, files={'file': open('sample.pdf','rb')}, data={'purpose':'document_ingest'})``
- Browser TS (FormData):
```ts
const form = new FormData();
form.append('file', fileInput.files[0]);
form.append('purpose', 'document_ingest');
const r = await fetch('/v1/uploads', { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` }, body: form });
console.log(await r.json());
```
Note in the doc: "Do not set Content-Type manually when using FormData in browsers."

maria: tiny nit: add a very small JSON-only example for "remote URL" uploads and explicitly call out that JSON is only for server-side fetches the service performs (not for raw binary). Example: { "url": "https://.../file.pdf", "purpose": "document_ingest" }.

adien: small correction: the runtime returns `storage_key` now (opaque string), and includes `metadata: { filename, size_bytes }`. Please update the response sample and add a migration blurb at top: "2026-03-27: uploads response `file_id` -> `storage_key`; examples now show multipart/form-data for binary uploads."

claire: adding changelog line and a link to SDK migration note. Also adding a short acceptance test in `docs/test/samples/uploads-smoke.md` that runs the curl example against local dev and asserts 2xx and presence of `storage_key` in response JSON.

sam: good. Also add a quick linkcheck exemption for the sample URL we use in the JSON example, or host a small placeholder in `docs/static/sample-files/` so linkcheck doesn't fail CI.

docs-bot: Checklist for PR #3599: markdown snippets added, openapi pending (adrien), changelog added, acceptance test added, linkcheck update pending.

adrien: pushed OpenAPI patch: added multipart/form-data, retained application/json for remote-url shape, included enum for purpose. Ran `openapi-cli validate` -> clean.

maria: reviewed wording + tests. small grammar nit fixed.

claire: pushed final changes and updated the SDK migration guide with a one-liner: "Replace `file_id` with `storage_key` for uploads; treat `storage_key` as an opaque identifier."

adrien: CI green, merging. ran the acceptance test locally (curl against local dev) and it returned 200 with `storage_key`.

sam: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short note in the releases channel for integrators so SDK teams can bump their examples.

claire: thanks all, closing the loop.
